text:
morgan: Kicking off a focused intra-node topology sweep comparing NVLink/SXM vs PCIe for multi-GPU inference. Goal: see KV-cache sharing and latency/throughput at different batch sizes and with/without NUMA pinning. region: us-west-2 (SXM nodes) vs us-east-1 (PCIe nodes).

infra-bot: benchmark-job queued: job_id=bench-1865012345, nodes=2xA100-SXM4(us-west-2), 2xA100-PCIE(us-east-1), model=redwood-7b, seq_len=512, batches=[1,4,8,16], runs=5

anya: nice. are you running with continuous batching and KV prefix caching enabled?

morgan: yes. default runtime batching enabled. doing two sub-experiments: (A) default (no explicit pinning), (B) numactl pinned process -> local numa node + CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES set and explicit interconnect prefetched. Also toggling INFER_PREFETCH=0/1.

rafa: reminder: for NUMA pinning use: 
```
numactl --cpunodebind=0 --membind=0 
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 
./run_infer --model redwood-7b --quant 4bit 
```
bind threads to GPUs' local CPU sockets to avoid cross-socket PCIe hops.

samir: pasted quick p50/p95 latencies and throughput (tokens/sec) from first pass (seq=512, quant=4bit):
- SXM (no pin): batch1 p50=62ms p95=120ms thr=230 tok/s
- SXM (pin+prefetch): batch1 p50=58ms p95=100ms thr=245 tok/s
- PCIe (no pin): batch1 p50=85ms p95=210ms thr=160 tok/s
- PCIe (pin+prefetch): batch1 p50=72ms p95=150ms thr=185 tok/s

samir: at batch8 the differences amplify:
- SXM (pin): p50=230ms p95=320ms thr=980 tok/s
- PCIe (pin): p50=410ms p95=780ms thr=620 tok/s

lina: interesting — p95 on PCIe spikes a lot at higher batches. did you see any host CPU saturated counters or PCIe stalls?

morgan: yes, on PCIe nodes iostat and nvidia-smi topo show intermittent host <-> device copy stalls. HW counters: PCIe Tx latency jitter up ~2.5x vs SXM. Also observed occasional memcpy CPU steal when kernel scheduled between sockets.

rafa: that matches prior microbenchmarks: NVLink reduces inter-GPU KV exchange latency and also keeps GPU-to-GPU transfers off the host. For model-sharded KV cache, that matters a lot at higher batch/sequence lengths.

anya: what about kernel selection? cuBLAS vs fused-attn/FLASH?

morgan: we used runtime auto-kernel selection. interestingly, SXM nodes favored fused attention kernels (reduced p50 by ~10%) while PCIe often fell back to fallback kernels for some layers when cross-GPU comms timed out. Enabling CUDA Graphs helped reduce p95 on SXM but had marginal wins on PCIe.

samir: added a short note on memory residency: when INFER_PREFETCH=1 we saw fewer page faults on SXM and slightly better p95. On PCIe prefetch helps but still suffers when host-to-device bandwidth bursts coincide with GC on host.

lina: any thermal or power differences? were PCIe nodes hitting power limits that throttle clocks?

morgan: slight throttling observed on one PCIe host under sustained batch16 runs — clocks dropped ~50 MHz for ~30s windows. SXM cluster was thermally stable. Could be chassis cooling + PCIe airflow.

rafa: suggestion: for production we should recommend mandatory NUMA pinning + prefetch for PCIe nodes, and prefer SXM for workloads relying on heavy inter-GPU KV sync or large batch sizes. Also add autoscaler hints to avoid co-locating cross-socket traffic heavy pods on PCIe hosts.

anya: can you dump the perf scripts and raw numbers to /shared/bench/1865012345? i'll use them for the perf playbook.

morgan: yep uploading CSVs + flamegraphs + nsys traces now. link: https://internal/bench/1865012345 (will post once upload completes).

infra-bot: upload complete: /shared/bench/1865012345 (csv,nsys,flamegraphs).

samir: next steps: run same sweep with sequence=1024 and with model shard (tensor-slicing) turned on. also try quantization=8-bit to see if increased compute pressure shifts crossover points between PCIe/SXM.

lina: if you need me i can run ambient temp checks and fan curves on the PCIe chassis.

morgan: thanks all — will run seq=1024 sweep tomorrow and ping when done. feel free to flag anything else to add to the run matrix. :rocket:
